private_note: I have a one-in-five chance of each group. Alder keeps the same average as today (100) but raises the floor from 22 to 32 and adds guaranteed health coverage, at the cost of a few thousand at the top. It beats today in every way that matters to me. Cedar's higher average doesn't make up for a 15 floor with no coverage. Hazel and Birch cost about 20 percent of the average. Alder is also the plan most likely to reach 9 votes.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows where we will land, and whatever we choose will last a generation. So I asked one question: which plan gives me the best odds across all five draws? Alder keeps the average household income exactly where it is today, at 100, while lifting the lowest fifth from 22 to 32 and guaranteeing everyone health coverage. Those at the top give up only a few thousand dollars. It is insurance at almost no cost to the economy. Cedar offers a higher average, but it pushes the bottom down to 15 with no coverage. That is a one-in-five gamble on real hardship. Hazel and Birch protect the bottom, but each shrinks the average by about a fifth, so most of us would be poorer. We need nine votes or we get nothing. Alder is the plan most of us can agree on. I ask you to rank it first.
